html:
Codex (GPT-6.1 Sol): disagree. "A promising research candidate", but the draft did not establish ≤ ₹0.40 without quality loss: it compared the candidate on real transcripts with today on perfect ones, counted half-price Flex as measured, and its one pass would change official pointer scores (AC-SVAL). Its paired bootstrap matched ours.

Gemini 3.8 Flash (agy): agree with changes. The cost diagnosis and the one-pass consolidation are sound; the "tomorrow" pipeline cannot be approved as written. It added what Codex missed: Gemini 3.8 Flash doubles in price on 1 Jan 2027, and GPT-6 Luna — already measured end to end — beats 3.8 Flash on facts, unsupported facts and cost.

Both reviewers flaggedChanged in v1.0
Candidate on real transcripts vs today on perfect ones; unsupported facts +4.9 points; no Scribe controlGate failure stated; today's pipeline re-run on the same Flash-Lite transcripts; Scribe control made a precondition
Flex never calledFlex numbers labelled projections; latency and fallbacks go into the shadow week
AC-SVAL and the audio data flowRecommended pipeline keeps today's pointer review; audio needs the owner's approval
Speaker attribution not validated; two "today" baselinesListed as limits; baselines explained, savings quoted against staging

Where they differ: Codex wants contract-preserving fixes first (dedupe, timer no-ops, compact JSON, caching); agy proposes silence trimming (it assumed 20–35% silence; staging audio measured 3–4%), caching, key compression and short-call triage. Errors they caught and that are fixed: the Luna end-to-end row was shown as pending though finished; Sarvam's retention mixed a credit-exhaustion failure with quality; cost fits paired the Flash-Lite transcript with the analysis measured on perfect transcripts. Full texts are in the repository.
